bibliographic_scope.title: Mass Spectrometric Study of Nanocrystalline ZnO Vaporization
bibliographic_scope.authors: A. V. Makarov; S. G. Zbezhneva; V. V. Kovalenko; M. N. Rumyantseva

source_interpretation.text: The gel preparation/decomposition gives the source nanocrystalline ZnO. Empty-cell cleaning, high-vacuum conditioning and hot vaporization belong to analysis; they do not supply additional growth schedules.
The authors interpret nanocr1 as metastable and nanocr2 as aged material with vaporization behavior closer to microcrystalline ZnO. No new particle size or storage atmosphere is reported.
The Zn+/O2+ signals cannot determine vapor molar composition because scattered oxygen gives uncontrolled background. The table ratio remains an instrumental observation.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Oxygen background and Table 2

analytical_context.mass_spectrometer: MI-1201; mass resolution1:1200; silver-referenced sensitivity4.8×10^-20 Pa cm2/(V K).
analytical_context.cell: Pt Knudsen cell; effusion-hole/cell cross-sectional area1:700. Empty-cell1550K6h before sample; loaded450K4h high vacuum.
analytical_context.background: H2O+/CO+ do not exceed 40–50mV at measurement start; Zn+ background≤10–15%. O2 background uncontrolled.
analytical_context.trace_ions: m/z80 observed around10^-5 of Zn+;82/84 absent, authors regard observed ZnO ion signal as accidental and calculate only upper pressure limits.
analytical_context.calibration: Ag vapor pressure calibration below Ag melting point to avoid cell reaction; conversion coefficient ratio gAg/gx=1 assumption; source molecular cross-section relation0.75×sum of atomic values.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Experimental and pressure calculation discussion

equations_context.2–4: Source ion-current/calibration/cross-section pressure model, variables and assumptions on p2; no new computation performed.

prior_literature_context.vapor_molecules: Earlier work reported0.04–0.06%ZnO molecules under disturbed molecular flow; source questions equilibrium relevance.
prior_literature_context.effusion_limit: Tentative upper10Pa corresponds total vapor overZnO at 1435K, cited background not synthesis.
prior_literature_context.table3: Two comparison columns calculated from references5/10; table footnote pO2=25.1Pa at 1435K belongs reference5.
prior_literature_context.table4: Reference11 row: p1.60×10^-3Pa at 1456K, enthalpy466±6.4 and dissociation258±6.5kJ/mol; reference12 row: upper4.3×10^-5Pa at 1468K, lower507 and upper217kJ/mol. Neither is a new preparation.

limitations: Complete supplied five-page main, Figure 1, Tables 1–5, equations 1–12 and all 12 numbered references. SI and cited full sources unreviewed.

The source gives precursor concentrations but not their volumes, mole ratio, hydroxide addition rate, gel aging, isolation/washing, decomposition atmosphere, heating ramp or yield. No quantities or cited-book procedures are supplied by inference.
Zinc nitrate hydration, reagent purities and the exact solution solvent are not named. Formula Zn(NO3)2 identifies the nominal solute; no hydrate formula is inferred.
The 20 nm Scherrer value belongs to the prepared nanocrystalline ZnO. No measured crystallographic polymorph, unit cell, particle morphology or atomic coordinates are supplied.
The one-year-later nanocr2 measurement has no storage environment or new post-storage size measurement. No fresh synthesis, retained 20 nm size, or growth time is inferred from that interval.

The empty platinum cell cleaning at 1550 K for 6 h precedes sample loading and is analytical apparatus conditioning, not ZnO synthesis. The later 450 K/4 h high-vacuum sample conditioning is characterization preparation.

Table 3 prints pressure-column headings with missing or unreadable scaling exponent in the supplied PDF rendering/text. Preserve exact coefficients and source image, with conversion to Pa unresolved. Do not derive the missing exponent from curves, fits or expected values.

Table 4 upper-limit inequality glyphs render poorly; the prose explicitly establishes upper pressure/dissociation limits and lower sublimation-enthalpy limits. Numerical bounds are retained as source limits, not exact measured values.

Formal Zn+/O2+ current ratios are not the molar Zn/O2 vapor composition: uncontrolled oxygen background prevents that determination. Quantitative reference comparisons and thermochemical inputs remain context, not new preparations.
